newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon patriarch says widespread arrests illegal.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon patriarch says widespread arrests illegal.

text.p: Lebanon's Maronite Patriarch Nasrallah Sfeir on Sunday questioned the legality of a wave of arrests of opposition figures in the country.

The Paris-based Rally for Lebanon (RPL) said people from all opposition groups had been detained. It put at 200 the number of people held after gunmen killed one Syrian worker in an attack on a Syrian van on Wednesday in the Christian area of Tabarja north of Beirut.

The patriarch, an outspoken critic of the pro-Syrian government, said that illegal persecution violated democratic principles, individual freedoms and the constitution, but he stopped short of directly accusing the government of breaking the law.

"Citizens question in anxiety and bitterness: Are there no legal principles of pursuit any more? Have security men been transformed into dawn visitors, with no identity and names, bashful of what they are doing?," he said.
Lebanese Christian opponents in Paris said on Sunday more dissidents were still being detained and called on French and other western leaders to intervene to put an end to the crackdown.
The RPL, which is close to exiled Lebanese former general Michel Aoun, said its members Samir Tayeh and Obad Zouein were among the latest to be arrested.
Two others, Youssef Salameh and Emile Hachem, escaped arrest as they were away from home when armed civilians stormed their home.
"The Lebanese government detains and tortures hundreds of political opponents instead of letting Lebanese justice do its work," the RPL said on Sunday.

"The RPL launches an urgent appeal to leaders of the free world, especially President Jacques Chirac, to intervene to put an end to the persecution of peaceful Lebanese whose only crime is to want their country's freedom," it said on Sunday.
There was no immediate reaction from the office of Chirac who is away from Paris on a Christmas holiday.

"How can we affirm on international platforms that Lebanon deeply believes in democratic principles and human rights and that the Lebanese constitution preserves individual freedom? It is a question that needs to be answered in deeds not in words," Sfeir said from Bkerki, north of Beirut.

Prosecutor general Adnan Addoum said on Saturday the detentions were legal and followed activities by "disruptive elements" who wanted to harm Lebanon's ties with brotherly countries, an apparent reference to Syria.
Syria is the main power broker in Lebanon and has some 35,000 troops in the country.
Sfeir said the church "denounces all forms of violence".
"We pray for our Lebanese sons and brothers to face with courage the persecution they are enduring these days which casts shadows of doubt and accusations on them".
The RPL said detainees were being accused of belonging to a pro-Israeli network in Lebanon, a charge carrying a possible death sentence.
Prosecutor Addoum said none of the detainees was officially charged and many were released on Friday.
